info.name: Incident Report — Backend API
info.description:
Backend API of the incident reporting system, for exercising it without a frontend.

**Start the system first** — from the repository root:

```
docker compose up --build
```

Every response saved as an example was captured from a running instance, not written by hand.

## How to use it

1. Send one of the requests under *Incident Reports → Submit*. Its test script stores the new id in the `reportId` collection variable.
2. *Read one* and the requests under *Error contract* then work with no copy-pasting.
3. Or press **Run** on the collection: every request carries assertions, so the whole thing doubles as a smoke test of the API.

## Submitting returns a receipt, not a result

`POST /incident-reports` answers with the report's id and when it arrived — nothing about what was extracted from it. That data belongs to the module that produces it and is read separately, through `GET /incidents?rawReportId=...` (T-16).

One extra request is the price. It buys the freedom to move analysis off the request thread, or onto a broker, without a single client having to change: the query simply answers "not analysed yet" for a while, and the live stream says when that changes.

Text extraction itself is not implemented yet, so every report is currently recorded as `OTHER` / `UNCLASSIFIED`, dated from its submission, with warnings saying so — the system's real behaviour for text it cannot recognise, not a placeholder. None of that appears in these responses yet, because the endpoint that serves it is still to come.

## Endpoints not in this collection yet

They are designed but not built, so they would only return 404 here:

- `GET /api/v1/incidents?rawReportId=...` — what was extracted from a report, and the traceability direction from raw text to records (T-16)
- `GET /api/v1/analytics/time-series`, `/analytics/summary` — chart data (T-17)
- `GET /api/v1/stream/incidents` — SSE stream (T-18)
- `POST /api/v1/incident-reports/{id}/reprocess` — re-run analysis (T-19)

See `docs/TASKS.md` for what each task delivers.

item.name: Health
item.description: Is the system up, and did it reach both databases?

request.description:
Reports the application together with each database as its own component, so a failure points at what is actually broken.

Component detail is switched on in the `local` and `docker` profiles only; the base configuration keeps it off.

item.name: Catalog
item.description:
What the system recognises, and where every choice in the interface comes from.

The frontend keeps no catalog of its own: if it did, adding an event type would mean a configuration change *and* a frontend release, and the two would drift apart in between. Labels travel with the keys for the same reason.

request.description:
Every event type with its metrics, plus the 81 provinces in plate-code order.

Adding an event type touches `backend/analysis/src/main/resources/incident-catalog.yml` and nothing else - no Java change and no migration. A catalog that fails validation stops the application at startup rather than letting it recognise less than it is configured to.

item.name: Reprocess — read the same text with today's rules

request.description: Runs the current extraction rules over a stored text again (FR-15). The raw text is not touched - it is the input, not the subject - and the records derived from it are replaced rather than added to, so running this twice leaves exactly what running it once leaves. The answer is the same receipt a submission returns: it says the request was accepted, not what was found. Read the new result with `Incidents -> By raw report`, exactly as after a submission.

request.description:
The only way to find out what a submission produced.

`POST /incident-reports` answers with an id and a timestamp - never with a result (ADR-021), because analysis is a separate concern from storing the text. This filter closes the loop, and it answers with both halves of the question in one request: the records, and whether analysis succeeded.

Sample 3 is the interesting one. It produces three records from one text: Bursa's own figures, Kocaeli's own figures, and the ten injured the text gives for both together. That last one belongs to no single province - it is never split between them and never dropped, so per-province totals and the overall total can still be reconciled (ADR-019).

request.description:
One record in full: its metrics, the provinces it covers, and the words the extractor reacted to.

Each keyword carries its role - what it was evidence for - and its position in the raw text. item.name: Error contract (RFC 7807)
item.description:
Every failure comes back as `application/problem+json`, whether it originates in the domain or in Spring itself.

Two fields matter to a client: `status`, and `code` — the stable, machine-readable identifier to branch on. `detail` is free to be reworded.

Each request here also asserts that nothing internal leaks: no exception type, no stack frame, no connection string.

request.description: Whitespace is not a report. Rejected by the service rather than by an annotation on the request, so the same rule also holds on the reprocessing path, which has no HTTP request behind it.

request.description: A well-formed id that matches nothing. The message names the resource and the id, and nothing else.
A failure raised by Spring rather than by the domain. It still comes back in the same shape — a client should not need two parsers for one API.

There is no delete endpoint and there will not be one; the raw text is an audit log.

Worth reading the `code`: it says `request.method-not-allowed`, not `request.malformed`. Telling a client its body was broken when the body was never the problem sends it looking in the wrong place.
The API speaks JSON. Anything else is refused before the body is looked at.
An id that matches nothing is a 404 carrying a problem document, not an empty body - the same contract every other endpoint answers with.
A well-formed id that belongs to nothing. Reprocessing is a command with a target, so there is only one honest answer when the target does not exist.
